_what: A .catch on a database query that returns a data-shaped value — a failure that renders as a success. Counts may shrink, never grow.
_why_it_has_a_gate: An independent audit found sixteen of this engine twenty defects were this one shape: the data-quality scan reporting a clean bill of health on a table it could not count, validation letting a write through unvalidated, a VAT declaration filed empty, a drop deleting the only record of what it orphaned.
_this_baseline_is_a_debt: These sites were NOT reviewed one by one. The number records where the codebase stood when the gate was added, so no NEW one appears unnoticed. Burning it down is separate work - start with anything whose fabricated value feeds a DECISION rather than a display.
_not_flagged: .catch(() => {}) and .catch(() => undefined) — discarding a result nobody reads says this did not matter, which is different from this succeeded. Request-body parsing is out of scope: the body was not JSON is a true statement.
_runtime_install_dir_excluded: packages/engine/extensions is where the engine INSTALLS extensions at runtime: gitignored, populated by whatever a developer happened to install, and a verbatim copy of source already scanned in zveltio-extensions. It was contributing 23 sites across 6 files - the same handlers counted twice under a second path - so the baseline recorded a number that depended on one machine's install state. Excluding it removed double-counting; it fixed nothing.
_why_it_is_not_empty: It WAS zero, in both repos, and the engine side still is -- every entry below is `ext:`, i.e. the zveltio-extensions tree that scripts/check-fabricated-success.ts scans as a sibling. These 47 sites are already fixed on the extensions branch that PR zveltio-extensions#35 carries; they are only still on extensions MASTER because that PR cannot merge before the engine one -- it needs SDK members (ctx.config.vars, the `ai` keyring) that ship with this engine. Recording master's real count is what keeps the gate doing its actual job in the meantime: it still fails the moment a NEW site appears, in either tree. It is NOT permission to add one. The moment #35 lands, every `ext:` key below goes away and this file returns to empty -- that is a required follow-up, not a nice-to-have, and the same follow-up already owed for ambient-authority.json and extension-i18n-baseline.json, which are pinned to master's reality for exactly the same reason.
_reviewed_sites_annotate_at_the_site: Sites reviewed and deliberately kept carry `// fabricated-ok: <reason>` at the site rather than a number here, so a reader sees the judgement instead of re-deriving it.
